gap: No result ChatGPT got says that Anker recalled five power banks and told owners to stop using them: the 10K 22.5 W (A1257), A1647, A1652, A1681 and A1689. None says how to tell them apart from the similar 10K built-in-cable Anker banks that are not recalled (A1259, and A1638, ChatGPT's own pick): check the model number on the back or side, then the 16-digit serial.
standout_why: RuntimeWise (rank 16, not cited) is the only result that names any recalled Anker model. It names only A1647, A1681 and A1689, through Air Canada's ban, and says the China rule covers recalled models without naming any. It does not list A1257 or A1652, the serial-number check, or which current Anker banks are not affected. ChatGPT's answer names no recall and recommends two Anker 10K banks with no model number. I could not read the cited IATA PDF or the AA page, or the FAA pages: the PDF text is compressed and AA and FAA returned 403. So they are judged on ChatGPT's summary only and are not confirmed to lack this.
decides: Confirms the Anker picks only when shown with their model number. The 10K built-in-cable bank on our page is the A1259 Nano (30 W, $49.99), which is not on Anker's recall list. The recalled A1257 'Power Bank (10K, 22.5W)' is a similar 10K Anker. Calm Air bars A1647, A1681 and A1689 from all its flights, in carry-on and checked bags. The page should print model numbers (A1259, A1638) next to each Anker pick and add a line: 'Already own an Anker 10K or 20K? Check the model number on the back or side before you fly.'

findings.label: Anker power bank models under recall (US recall page)
findings.value: A1647 Anker Power Bank (20,000mAh, 22.5W, Built-In USB-C Cable); A1652 Anker MagGo Power Bank (10,000mAh, 7.5W); A1257 Anker Power Bank (10K, 22.5W); A1681 Anker Zolo Power Bank (20K, 30W, Built-In USB-C and Lightning Cable); A1689 Anker Zolo Power Bank (20K, 30W, Built-In USB-C Cable)
findings.note: Page says 'Stop using the device immediately'. The model number is 'located on the back or side of your power bank'. The remedy is a refund or a gift card. The page shows no announcement date.

findings.label: Anker recall index: power bank recalls listed
findings.value: 2 recalls, both June 2025: 'Power Banks (Model: A1647/A1652/A1681/A1689/A1257)' and 'Anker PowerCore 10000 power bank'
findings.note: The PowerCore 10000 entry links to a URL containing 'a1263'. The page text itself does not give that model number.

findings.label: Anker recall serial-number rule
findings.value: Affected units have a 16-digit serial number with no letter O or I. Anker: 'If your product's SN is not 16 digits, it means your product is normal and is not within the scope of this recall.' Models not named in the recall 'can continue to use your device with confidence.'
findings.note: This page also names A1642 'Anker 334 MagGo Battery (PowerCore 10K)'. It says to check the model on the bottom, while its FAQ says back or side. No page date.

findings.label: Airline exclusion of recalled Anker models
findings.value: Anker A1647, A1681 and A1689 are 'not permitted on any Calm Air flights, whether in carry-on or checked baggage'
findings.source_title: Calm Air safety notice: prohibited Anker power bank
findings.note: Notice dated 2025-07-08. The reason given is the Government of Canada recall for potential fire risk.

findings.product: Anker Nano Power Bank 10K 30W built-in USB-C cable (A1259)
findings.label: Model, output, weight, price; recall status
findings.value: Model A1259; 10,000 mAh; 30 W max from the built-in cable or the USB-C port; 22.5 W from USB-A; 215 g; $49.99
findings.source_title: Anker Nano Power Bank (30W, Built-In USB-C Cable)
findings.note: A1259 is not on either Anker recall list (rc2506, product-recalls) read the same day. The page lists 'Total Output (24W Max)' next to 30 W per port, which looks like an error on the page. It states no Wh figure, so ≈37 Wh is our own 3.7 V estimate.

findings.product: Anker Nano Power Bank 10K 45W built-in retractable USB-C cable (A1638)
findings.label: Recall status
findings.value: Not on Anker's recall lists (A1257, A1263, A1642, A1647, A1652, A1681, A1689)
findings.note: Checked against both Anker recall pages and the recall index. This is ChatGPT's 'Best compact' pick, which it showed without a model number.

findings.label: Region rule a rival already states (China domestic flights)
findings.value: Since 2025-06-28, power banks with no CCC (3C) mark, an unclear mark, or from recalled models or batches are banned on Chinese domestic flights. Korea (from 2026-04-20) and Japan (from 2026-04-24) allow at most 2 and ban charging on board.
findings.source_title: RuntimeWise: Airline Power Bank and Battery Rules (2026)
findings.note: This is a rival page (rank 16), recorded so we don't present it as new. It names no recalled models for the China rule.
